open_points.subject: A01 create-repeat invariant
open_points.text:
create(m, request_id = k, facts = f) where existing r of m has r.request_id = k:
  rights fail or project archived => refused, store unchanged
open_points.question: Does “project archived” apply only to room and pointer creates, or also to a repeated project create, which rule 4 and Required test 4 require to answer the archived project?
options: Limit the archived-project refusal to adding rooms and publishing pointers
Refuse every repeated create associated with an archived project
Remove the special case and rely on each operation's stated admission rules
open_points.default_guess: Limit the archived-project refusal to adding rooms and publishing pointers.

witness.initial: An active project was created with request id K and was later archived.
events: The owner repeats 'create a project' with request id K and the original facts.
outcomes: A01 Required test 4: Registry answers the archived project and changes nothing.
A01's formal invariant: Registry refuses because the project is archived.

open_points.subject: A01 request-id form
open_points.text: printable text of at most 128 characters
open_points.question: Which characters are printable, and what unit is used for the 128-character limit?
options: Printable ASCII, counted as bytes/ASCII characters
Unicode characters excluding control and separator characters, counted as Unicode code points
Any nonblank Unicode text, counted as Unicode code points
open_points.default_guess: Printable ASCII with a maximum of 128 characters.

witness.initial: A caller has generated a request id containing 128 non-ASCII printable characters.
events: The caller submits a create using that request id.
outcomes: Registry accepts it because it contains 128 Unicode code points.
Registry refuses it because request ids are restricted to printable ASCII or exceed a byte-based limit.

open_points.subject: A16 migration file digest
open_points.text:
The mapping names
the file by its digest.
open_points.question: What digest algorithm, byte domain and textual representation define the file identity used by the mapping, confirmation, closure and audit entry, and what collision guarantee is required?
options: SHA-256 of the exact uploaded file-part bytes, encoded as lowercase hexadecimal
SHA-256 of a canonicalized parsed import representation
Another release-fixed digest algorithm and encoding
open_points.default_guess: SHA-256 of the exact uploaded file-part bytes, encoded as lowercase hexadecimal.

witness.initial: Two upload byte streams parse to the same import records but differ in whitespace or encoding.
events: The owner uploads the first file and sees its mapping.
The owner uploads the second file and attempts to confirm the first mapping.
outcomes: The files have different identities because the digest covers exact uploaded bytes.
The files have the same identity because the digest covers canonical parsed content.
witness.observer: The owner and the stored migration closure

open_points.subject: A16 import transaction timestamps
open_points.text:
A Customer the import makes is
  created at the import's instant with revision 1.
open_points.question: Must the new Customers, migration closure and audit entry written by one accepted import share one clock reading, or may each receive a separately read instant?
options: Read once and use the same instant for every fresh timestamp of the import transaction
Read separately for each created record
Read once per record category
open_points.default_guess: Read once and use the same instant throughout the transaction.

witness.initial: An import begins immediately before a clock tick or UTC date boundary.
events: Registry creates Customers, the closure and the audit entry in one transaction.
outcomes: Every newly written fact carries one identical import instant.
Customers, closure and audit entry carry different instants from separate clock readings.
witness.observer: The owner reading the imported Customers and audit log

open_points.subject: State 2 time authority and representation
open_points.text:
Every "today" in Registry is the current date in UTC, as every
instant is (L16).
open_points.question: What authoritative source supplies current time, what precise aware-datetime representation and precision are used, and how many readings does each operation take?
options: An injected UTC clock, one reading per operation, stored as timezone-aware UTC datetimes at fixed precision
A declared authority module, with each timestamp request reading it independently
A datetime supplied explicitly to every operation, normalized to a fixed UTC precision
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected UTC clock, read once per operation, and normalize to timezone-aware UTC datetimes at microsecond precision.

witness.initial: An operation starts just before midnight UTC and writes or compares more than one time-dependent fact.
events: The operation validates a value against today.
The operation writes its result and audit facts after midnight.
outcomes: One clock reading makes validation and every written timestamp belong to the same operation instant/date.
Separate readings make validation use one date while stored facts use another.
witness.observer: The owner and any test around the UTC boundary

open_points.subject: State 6 clock contract
open_points.text: Every time Registry records is an instant in UTC with time zone (L16).
open_points.question: Once State 2 fixes the authority and reading semantics, how does each timestamp-writing operation receive that authority in its exact contract?
options: A datetime parameter on each mutating operation
A clock port supplied through __init__
A declared authority module used by timestamp-writing modules
consequences: A datetime parameter makes readings explicit per call but expands every mutation contract.
A clock port centralizes time and supports deterministic tests while preserving operation-level control.
An authority module reduces parameters but introduces a process-wide dependency.
open_points.requirement: every mutating operation that writes a fresh timestamp receives the time source State 2 decided, in its contract (a datetime parameter, a clock port in __init__, or a declared authority module)

open_points.subject: A09 disclosure-class invariant
open_points.text:
class(answer(op)) <= highest_class(s)
highest_class(Cabinet Kernel) = business_confidential
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must show both the general answer-class ceiling and that Cabinet Kernel's ceiling is exactly business_confidential? Test 2 can refuse Kernel's context call solely because `context` is absent from Kernel's operation row.
options: Add a table-wide test that every allowed operation's possible answers are at or below its service ceiling
Add focused tests for every operation capable of returning personal_data, including an operation Kernel otherwise may call
Bind the invariant to a generated policy check that explicitly asserts both statements
open_points.default_guess: Add a table-wide policy test and a focused Kernel boundary test.

open_points.subject: A22 first-release vocabulary invariant
open_points.text: declared_types(first release) = {estimate -> PresuPro}
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must show that the first release declares exactly `estimate` and maps it to PresuPro, rather than merely showing that `wall_plan` is unknown?
options: Assert the complete first-release mapping
Assert the derived manifest and runtime mapping both equal the complete mapping
Test only publication of estimate and rejection of one undeclared example
open_points.default_guess: Assert that both the runtime vocabulary and derived manifest equal the complete mapping.

open_points.subject: A22 vocabulary-change preservation invariant
open_points.text: pointers are never removed or rewritten by a vocabulary change
open_points.question: Must the required test compare every fact of every affected pointer before and after the release change, or only show that pointers remain listed with their statuses?
options: Compare every pointer fact before and after the vocabulary change
Compare identity and status only
Require only that the pointers remain listable
open_points.default_guess: Compare every pointer fact before and after the vocabulary change.

open_points.subject: A19 rendering invariant
open_points.text: render(v) = escape(v) for every stored value v
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must establish escaping for every rendering context that can display a stored value, rather than only room names and access-request text?
options: A context-complete test matrix for HTML text, attributes and every other rendering context used
A property test over every owner-interface presenter
Keep the two examples as sufficient witnesses
open_points.default_guess: Use a context-complete test matrix over every owner-interface presenter.

open_points.subject: A19 interpreted-input invariant
open_points.text: no stored value is ever evaluated or executed
open_points.question: Which Required tests item must show that caller and import values cannot alter query, command or template structure or otherwise be evaluated?
options: Tests for each interpreted boundary and fixed-alternative selector
A structural factory check plus representative runtime injection tests
Treat the quote-and-semicolon round trip as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Require a structural check and representative runtime tests for every interpreted boundary.

open_points.subject: A19 browser script prohibition
open_points.text:
The owner interface sends no script of its own (R0-29) and forbids the
   browser to run any, by its content security policy.
open_points.question: What Required tests item must show both that responses contain no application script and that the effective content security policy prohibits script execution?
options: Assert response bodies and the exact effective CSP on every owner-interface response
Use a browser test proving inline and external scripts do not execute
Use both header assertions and a browser execution test
open_points.default_guess: Use both header assertions and a browser execution test.

open_points.subject: A19 multipart-head bound
open_points.text:
at most the imported
   `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` constant
open_points.question: What release-fixed value does `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES` have, and exactly which bytes before the file part count toward it?
options: 64 KiB covering all multipart bytes received before the first file byte
1 MiB covering all multipart bytes received before the first file byte
Another explicit release-fixed byte limit
open_points.default_guess: 64 KiB covering every received multipart byte before the file part's content.

witness.initial: A valid upload has an unusually large CSRF field or multipart headers before a small file.
events: The owner submits the multipart upload.
outcomes: Registry admits the request because its pre-file head is within the chosen bound.
Registry refuses it because another implementation chose a smaller bound or counted different framing bytes.

open_points.subject: A02 required-value invariant
open_points.text: for every stored required value v: not missing(v)
open_points.question: Which Required tests must show the invariant for every required-value source, including object address, Customer name and kind, and session access-request text?
options: A test matrix covering every required field and every operation that supplies it
A property test parameterized by the required-field catalogue
Keep the project-name and room-name examples as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Add a parameterized test covering every required field and supplying operation.

open_points.subject: A02 numeric domain
open_points.text:
a floor area not
   greater than zero, a number of rooms that is not a whole number of at
   least 1, or a floor that is not a whole number
open_points.question: Which numeric domain and wire forms do the fields accept, including whether non-finite values, exponent notation and numerically integral decimals are admissible?
options: Finite JSON numbers, with rooms and floor requiring mathematically integral values
Decimal strings in a canonical format
Integer wire types for rooms and floor and a finite decimal wire type for area
open_points.default_guess: Use integer wire types for rooms and floor and a finite decimal type for area.
consequences: Generic JSON numbers require explicit rejection of NaN and infinity and a rule for values such as 2.0.
Canonical decimal strings preserve exact written values but change the public field representation.
Separate integer and finite-decimal types make the form constraints structural.
open_points.requirement: No accepted requirement states the admissible numeric wire representation or whether non-finite values are allowed.

open_points.subject: A16 imported-instant syntax
open_points.text: an instant cannot be read
open_points.question: What exact import syntax, precision and offset rules make an instant readable?
options: RFC 3339 timestamps with an explicit offset, normalized to UTC
Only canonical timestamps ending in Z at fixed precision
The exact legacy v1 timestamp syntax, with an explicit normalization rule
open_points.default_guess: Accept the documented legacy v1 syntax with an explicit offset and normalize it to canonical UTC.
consequences: Broad RFC 3339 acceptance eases migration but permits multiple textual forms for one instant.
Canonical Z-only input simplifies validation but may reject legacy exports.
Legacy-specific parsing preserves migration compatibility but must be fully declared and tested.
open_points.requirement: Every time Registry records is an instant in UTC with time zone (L16).

open_points.subject: A01 owner-interface request-id generation
open_points.text:
The owner interface makes
   one when it renders a create form
open_points.question: Which generator and encoding does the owner interface use to produce a printable request id from at least 16 random bytes, and is the same id preserved across a form resubmission?
options: UUIDv4 generated once per rendered form and carried unchanged on resubmission
Base64url encoding of 16 or more cryptographically random bytes
A longer cryptographically random token encoded as lowercase hexadecimal
open_points.default_guess: Generate one UUIDv4 per rendered form and preserve it across resubmissions of that form.
consequences: UUIDv4 is interoperable and compact but its fixed version and variant bits affect the literal entropy interpretation.
Base64url preserves compact random bytes but requires an explicit accepted alphabet.
Hexadecimal is simplest to validate but produces longer identifiers.
open_points.requirement: an opaque value the caller makes, unique for every create it means as new — printable text of at most 128 characters, made from at least 16 random bytes, as a random UUID is

open_points.subject: R0-96 agent instruction installation
open_points.text:
adding the rule there is the
platform's change, made before the first release goes into production.
open_points.question: What later-layer check proves that the required room-name and alias rule is present in the agent-home instructions actually deployed before production admission?
options: A factory check parses the generated AGENTS.md and requires the rule
A deployment check verifies the installed file and its approved digest
Factory generation and deployment verification both enforce it
open_points.default_guess: Use both a factory content check and deployment verification of the installed file.
consequences: A factory-only check proves the produced artifact but not that the admitted artifact was installed.
A deployment-only check can verify installation but may discover omissions late.
Both checks cover artifact creation and the production installation boundary.
open_points.requirement:
In the first
release the agent learns it from its instructions, which the platform
installs in the agent's home on the home server (Factory
`platform/home_server/workspace/AGENTS.md`); adding the rule there is the
platform's change, made before the first release goes into production.

open_points.subject: A09 service-rights policy
open_points.text:
Registry knows from its own release
   which operations that service may call and the highest disclosure class it
   may receive (R0-26, R0-27).
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The passage must name the service-rights and class table through its permitted generated-code path, such as an imported data-provider policy constant, rather than saying only that it comes from the release.

open_points.subject: A22 artifact vocabulary policy
open_points.text:
The declared types are part of the specification and of the release; a
   running instance reads them from its release, never from its configuration
   or its store (R0-33).
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The passage must place the closed type-to-owner-service mapping on one permitted path to generated code—model enumeration for the closed type names and an imported policy constant for the mapping—instead of introducing “the release” as an unnamed path.
